scope: Bounded primary-source review for the genuine 4D hypercube shadow and known-transform observability check
execution_policy: Read-only source inspection. No upstream code execution, deployment, external communication, human study, Gate 4/5D research, or UI work.

primary_sources.title: Dimensions, Chapters 3 and 4: The fourth dimension
sections_or_page_pins: Web page sections 2–3 (lines 16–42 in the fetched page): a point in 4D is represented by four coordinates; the table lists the 4D hypercube/tesseract with 16 vertices and 32 edges.
Web page section 4 (lines 43–58): sections and shadows are complementary ways to represent 4D objects; a 4D object can cast a changing 3D shadow as it turns in 4D.
Web page section 5 (lines 59–70): S³ is represented in R⁴ and stereographically projected to a 3D tangent space; passage through the projection pole produces an unbounded/infinite display.
The page title explicitly says Chapters 3 and 4; the browser tool exposed this combined page rather than a separate chapter-4 document.
supports: A 4D point requires four coordinates in the mathematical model.
The regular 4D hypercube/tesseract has 16 vertices and 32 edges.
A controlled turn of a 4D object can change its 3D shadow, and the shadow carries only partial information from any one view.
A stereographic-style 4D-to-3D representation needs an explicit projection-pole/infinity policy.
does_not_support: The Looking Glass rotation matrix, composition order, orthographic matrix P, or display-camera implementation.
A claim that one or more screenshots uniquely determine an arbitrary 4D object.
The rank-four reconstruction result for known transforms and correspondences; that is derived and checked in this project.
Human understanding, participant performance, semantic meaning, or physical extra dimensions.
primary_sources.use_in_gate3: Motivates the genuine 4-coordinate/16-vertex/32-edge object and the separate moving-shadow view, while retaining the source's warning that one shadow is partial information.

primary_sources.title: NumCS(E), AT’25, Chapter 3: Direct Methods for Linear Least Squares Problems
primary_sources.author: Ralf Hiptmair, ETH Zurich
sections_or_page_pins: §3.1.2, Theorem 3.1.2.1, PDF p. 9 / printed p. 222: x is a least-squares solution of Ax=b iff it satisfies AᵀAx=Aᵀb.
§3.1.2, Corollary 3.1.2.13 and Remark 3.1.2.15, PDF p. 12 / printed p. 225: if N(A)={0}, the least-squares solution is unique and x=(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀb; N(A)={0} is equivalent to rank(A)=n for m≥n.

§3.1.2, Remark 3.1.2.18 and the full-rank problem statement, PDF pp. 13–14 / printed pp. 226–227: rank loss means redundant, non-identifiable parameters; full rank defines the unique least-squares problem.
supports: For a stacked known linear system A q≈b, full column rank is the condition for a unique least-squares recovery of q.
The normal equations provide the bounded recovery check under the declared Euclidean model.
Rank deficiency means that different parameter vectors can yield the same outputs, so a fixed view can leave a hidden coordinate unobservable.
does_not_support: Recovery from arbitrary images or unknown point correspondences.
Recovery when transforms are unknown, nonlinear, or estimated from the same observations.
A physical or ontological claim about four-dimensional space, or a human-use result.
The project's specific x–w rotation or the separate display-camera control.
primary_sources.use_in_gate3: Provides the primary university reference for interpreting rank(P)=3 in a static/camera-only observation and rank([P R_k])=4 as a sufficient condition for unique numerical recovery with known transforms and correspondences.

unavailable_or_unresolved.note: The supplied prompt linked the combined Chapters 3–4 page above. This separate chapter-4 URL was derived for a bounded availability check, attempted once, and returned an access error. No content from it is used; do not infer page-specific claims from the unavailable URL.

derived_checks.derivation: Vertices are {-1,+1}^4, giving 2^4=16. Each vertex has four one-coordinate neighbors, so the undirected edge count is 16·4/2=32.
derived_checks.status: direct derivation under the declared object; Dimensions independently lists 16 vertices and 32 edges

derived_checks.claim: Static and camera-only observations have rank at most three
derived_checks.derivation: With P=[I₃ 0], a static observation has matrix P and rank 3. A known ordinary display camera C_k∈SO(3) gives C_k P; left multiplication by invertible C_k preserves row space, so stacking camera-only views remains rank 3 and cannot identify w.
derived_checks.status: direct linear-algebra derivation; no external claim needed

derived_checks.claim: An additional proper x–w rotation can give rank four
derived_checks.derivation: For column vectors R_xw(θ) has x′=cosθ·x−sinθ·w and w′=sinθ·x+cosθ·w. Stacking P at θ=0 with P R_xw(π/2) includes the rows e_xᵀ,e_yᵀ,e_zᵀ and −e_wᵀ, hence rank 4. The least-squares uniqueness interpretation then follows from the ETH full-column-rank result.
derived_checks.status: direct derivation plus bounded application of the ETH source

derived_checks.claim: Coincident pair separates under source rotation
derived_checks.derivation: For q_a=(a,b,c,w_a) and q_b=(a,b,c,w_b), Pq_a=Pq_b at θ=0. After R_xw(θ), their projected x difference is −sinθ·(w_a−w_b); θ=π/2 separates any unequal w values while preserving IDs.
derived_checks.status: direct derivation under the declared projection/rotation convention

limits: The review has two usable external sources, within the requested 2–4 source bound.
The mathematical observability result is conditional on exact known transforms, known point correspondences, an orthographic P, and numerical tolerance; it is not arbitrary shape reconstruction.
A rank result establishes model-level identifiability under those assumptions, not that a viewer can infer the property from an unfamiliar animation.
